title: BiMaCoSR: Binary One-Step Diffusion Model Leveraging Flexible Matrix Compression for Real Super-Resolution
page_convention: 1-based PDF pages; printed paper pages unless explicitly stated otherwise
summary: The auxiliary-overhead statement needs qualification by comparison baseline; initialization order differs between text and figure/release. The total compression ratios remain arithmetically consistent.
supported_impact: Two Minor concerns; neither a historical image-quality failure nor a measured hardware slowdown is established.

problems.title: Auxiliary overhead is not negligible relative to the binary baseline

original_claim.location: Abstract p1; Equation2 p4; Section3.5 p5; Table3(a) p8
original_claim.text: LRMB and SMB storage/computation overhead can be ignored.

assumptions: Use the paper's equivalent-operation and effective-parameter accounting.
Compare BMB with BMB plus LRMB in Table3(a); printed totals are rounded.
Equation2 compares full-precision low-rank storage with binary-branch storage.
problems.check: The increments are (1.83-0.78)/0.78=134.615% and (4.98-3.69)/3.69=34.959%. The square-matrix storage ratio 2Br/n retains the precision factor B.
problems.result: LRMB overhead is substantial relative to BMB. Total reduction ratios 50.23/1.83=27.448 and 118.59/4.98=23.813 remain correct.
counterevidence: The paper discloses the totals and acknowledges the rank/complexity tradeoff.
The added cost can be small relative to the full-precision baseline.
The SMB increment is not visible at the printed precision.
problems.impact: Minor scope/accounting overstatement; total compression advantage and image quality are not disproved.

correction.statement: Specify the comparison baseline and include auxiliary costs in compressed-model comparisons.
correction.verification: Arithmetic and scoped interpretation checked; no empirical repair.

problems.title: Text and figure/release reverse the initialization order

original_claim.location: Section3.4 pp4–5, Equations5–8, versus Figure3 p4 and ours.py654–667
original_claim.text: The text uses low-rank extraction first, while the figure and release use sparse extraction first.

assumptions: Both branches are enabled at rank8; k=2 max(input channels,output channels).
The 160 by160 matrix is an admissible finite weight matrix, with r=8 and k=320.
This is a mathematical decomposition diagnostic; no author code or trained model was run.
problems.check: Construct W_ij=sin((i+1)(j+2))+0.03(i+1)+0.007(j+1)+diag(160,...,1). The two orders give Frobenius differences L=434.6541495, S=420.9855802, R=135.1607553, and a quantized weight-sum difference of106.0913795.
problems.result: The orders do not commute. Both unquantized sums reconstruct W to numerical precision, while branch parameters and quantized weight sums differ.
counterevidence: Figure3 and the release agree; this is not a whole-paper/code contradiction.
Both orders are coherent decomposition procedures.
The historical order and metric effect are unestablished.
The weight-sum diagnostic is not a full forward pass including activation quantization.
problems.impact: Minor reproducibility and method-specification discrepancy; no historical score loss demonstrated.

correction.statement: Choose one documented order across equations, figure and code, and identify the historical order.
correction.verification: Non-equivalence established; no retraining or author adoption.

limitations: No training, restoration, author-code execution, raw-metric recomputation or hardware benchmark.
Historical code, configuration and checkpoint correspondence is unestablished.
The separate supplement is an author release with unverified historical publisher correspondence; extra OpenReview attachments were unavailable.
External references, later errata and the complete operation-count implementation were not comprehensively audited.
unresolved_claims: Historical image-quality effect of initialization order.
Real hardware latency and memory costs.
repair_verification: Baseline arithmetic clarified; non-equivalent initialization orders verified. No full-model repair or author adoption.
